en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban and Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> during an illness which had spread and there did not remain from him<sup>asws</sup> except for his<sup>asws</sup> head (as unaffected). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! It is very frequently what I<sup>asws</sup> am saying, what is upon a man whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to recognise this matter (Al-Wilayah), if he were to be at the top of a mountain until the death comes to him?

O Fuzay Bin Yasaar! The people are taking to the right and the left, and we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and our<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Shia, we are Guided to the Straight Path. O Fuzayl Bin Yasaar”

The Momin, if there happens to be for him, what is between the east and the west, it would be better for him, and if he was to become of cut off limbs, that would be better for him. O Fuzayl Bin Yasaar! Allahazwj does not Do with the Momin except for what is better for him.
O Fuzayl Bin Yasaar! Had the world in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> equated to a wing of a fly, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not have Quenched His<sup>azwj</sup> enemies from it a drink of water.

O Fuzayl Bin Yasaar! The one who concerns himself with one concern, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Suffice his concern, and the one whose concern was in every valley, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would not Care in which valley he perishes’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Faddalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Umar ibn Aban and Sayf ibn abu ‘Amirah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“Once I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) in his illness that he endured and nothing was left of him except his head (due to weakness). The Imam said, I very often O Fudayl, say, ‘A man to whom Allah grants belief in this cause (our Divine Authority) will have no trouble even if he were to live on a mountain until the coming of his death.
O Fudayl ibn Yasar, people took to the right and left, but our Shi’a (followers) and we found guidance in the right path.

O Fudayl ibn Yasar, for a believer it (belief) is better than his having all that is between the East and West. It (belief) is better for him even if he is cut in pieces. O Fudayl ibn Yasar, Allah does not do anything to believers except what is best for them.
O Fudayl ibn Yasar, had the world been worth the wing of a fly, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, would not have allowed His enemies to drink even a drop of water from it.

O Fudayl ibn Yasar, whoever finds one goal (the true belief) Allah suffices him in all other goals (affairs), however, one who has a goal in every valley Allah will be concerned the least where he may perish.’”
